headline: Legal win cushions a volume-driven profit decline
summary_short: Net revenue fell 3.3% y/y to $568.3 million on a 4.5% volume decline, while a favorable litigation-judgment reversal helped diluted EPS reach $4.96, down 9.0% y/y but a sharp swing from the $13.88 per-share loss booked in Q1.
summary_long: Boston Beer's quarter was shaped by the Ardagh supplier-dispute litigation: an amended judgment cut pre-judgment interest, producing an $18.0 million net pretax benefit versus the $216.0 million charge taken in Q1. Underlying demand was soft — net revenue fell 3.3% y/y to $568.3 million as shipment volume dropped 4.5% (led by Twisted Tea, Truly, Samuel Adams, Hard Mountain Dew), partly offset by pricing and mix. Advertising and promotional spending rose 16.4% y/y to $185.9 million, or 32.7% of revenue versus 27.2%, pressuring margins even as per-barrel cost of goods held flat. Cash rose to $265.5 million; the company continued buybacks, with about $174 million of authorization left, and now estimates full-year tariff costs of $20-30 million.

drivers.explanation: Revenue fell as shipment volume dropped 4.5% (Twisted Tea, Truly, Samuel Adams, Hard Mountain Dew all down), partially offset by favorable product mix and higher pricing.
An amended court judgment cut pre-judgment interest, producing an $18.0M net pretax benefit this quarter versus the $216.0M litigation charge booked in Q1 tied to the Ardagh supplier dispute.
Advertising and promotional spending rose 16.4% to 32.7% of revenue (from 27.2%), driven by higher local marketing investment and freight rates, pressuring operating margin.
Cost per barrel was roughly flat as aluminum- and tariff-driven inflation of $19.2M was offset by brewery efficiencies and contract renegotiation savings.
